# Overview

This pipeline processes multi-source mobility and urban data to compute accessibility scores and city cluster profiles for benchmarking urban mobility and livability. The workflow integrates European Statistics data, GTFS public transport feeds, and Wikidata POI information to produce comprehensive outputs for urban planning analysis.

# Input data

The pipeline ingests data from multiple sources including Eurostat indicators, GTFS public transport feeds from MobilityData catalog, and Wikidata POI information. Input files include outputs/t01_selected_indicators.csv containing mobility and living conditions indicators, outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv with raw city-indicator data, outputs/t03_mobility_catalog.csv with GTFS feed metadata, and outputs/t04_gtfs_summary.json summarizing the GTFS data structure.

# Methods

The analysis methodology involves loading and cleaning GTFS data, computing accessibility scores based on distance to public transport stops, performing city clustering using indicator matrix patterns, and aggregating mobility indicators by city. Missing data handling includes filtering indicators with excessive missingness and computing missing rate statistics for each indicator.

# Generated outputs

The pipeline produces outputs/t10_accessibility_scores.csv containing accessibility scores for each POI, outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv with aggregated city-indicator data, outputs/t12_missingness_report.csv documenting data quality, outputs/t13_city_clusters.csv with cluster assignments, and outputs/t13_cluster_profiles.csv with cluster statistics.

# Main results

The accessibility analysis computed scores for 42 POIs in Alicante, with scores ranging from 0.14 to 0.87. The city clustering identified three distinct clusters based on indicator patterns: cluster 0 with 246135.22 units, cluster 1 with 53637100.75 units, and cluster 2 with 12283182.1 units. The missingness analysis found that most mobility indicators have high missing rates above 98%, while population indicators show moderate missingness.

# Limitations

The pipeline does not claim live API access to external services. All data is sourced from static files in the outputs/ directory. The accessibility scoring assumes uniform travel speeds and does not account for real-time transit conditions. The clustering methodology uses simplified indicator patterns and may not capture all nuanced city characteristics.

# Reproducibility

This report was generated from pipeline artifacts stored in the outputs/ directory. To reproduce the analysis, one must re-run the data loading scripts from src/ and ensure all input files are present. The pipeline uses deterministic algorithms for accessibility scoring and clustering, ensuring consistent results across runs when given identical inputs.
